  # This agent can read the filesystem or fetch URLs\n        finder_agent = Agent(\n            name=\u0026quot;finder\u0026quot;,\n            instruction=\u0026quot;\u0026quot;\u0026quot;You can agents using capabilities exposed by \u003cstrong\u003eMCP\u003c/strong\u003e (Model Context Protocol) servers.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eMCP is quite low-level, and this framework handles the mechanics of connecting to servers, working with LLMs, handling external signals (like human input) and supporting persistent state via durable execution. That lets you, the developer, focus on the core business logic of your AI application.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eCore benefits:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e🤝 \u003cstrong\u003eInteroperability\u003c/strong\u003e: ensures that any tool exposed by any number of MCP servers can seamlessly plug in to your agents.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e⛓️ \u003cstrong\u003eComposability \u0026amp; Customizability\u003c/strong\u003e: Implements well-defined workflows, but in a composable way that enables compound workflows, and allows full customization across model provider, logging, orchestrator, etc.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e💻 \u003cstrong\u003eProgrammatic control flow\u003c/strong\u003e: Keeps things simple as developers just write code instead of thinking in graphs, nodes and edges. For branching logic, you write \u003ccode\u003eif\u003c/code\u003e statements. For cycles, use \u003ccode\u003ewhile\u003c/code\u003e loops.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e🖐️ \u003cstrong\u003eHuman Input \u0026amp; Signals\u003c/strong\u003e: Supports pausing workflows for external signals, such as human input, which are exposed as tool calls an Agent can make.\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cdiv class=\"markdown-heading\" dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003ch3 tabindex=\"-1\" class=\"heading-element\" dir=\"auto\"\u003eDo you need an MCP client to use mcp-agent?\u003c/h3\u003e\u003ca id=\"user-content-do-you-need-an-mcp-client-to-use-mcp-agent\" class=\"anchor\" aria-label=\"Permalink: Do you need an MCP client to use mcp-agent?\" href=\"#do-you-need-an-mcp-client-to-use-mcp-agent\"\u003e\u003csvg data-component=\"Octicon\" class=\"octicon octicon-link\" viewBox=\"0 0 16 16\" version=\"1.1\" width=\"16\" height=\"16\" aria-hidden=\"true\"\u003e\u003cpath d=\"m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z\"\u003e\u003c/path\u003e\u003c/svg\u003e\u003c/a\u003e\u003c/div\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eNo, you can use mcp-agent anywhere, since it handles MCPClient creation for you.
